history.dynasty: Antiquity uncertain; in the Kongu region of the Cheras
history.period: Over 500 years old per tradition; praised by Arunagirinathar in the Tirupugazh (15th century)
history.summary: The Thindal Murugan Temple crowns Thindal Malai, a ~50-metre hillock on the Coimbatore-Erode highway about 8 km from the Erode bus stand on Perundurai road. Thindal was one of the 24 regions of ancient Kongunadu, ruled by the Chera kings, and the temple is counted among the 108 Murugan temples praised in Arunagiriar's Tirupugazh hymns. The hill's ancient names - Thindalpalayam, Thindalmangalam, Thindalgiri, Melaithindal - are recorded in rock-cut inscriptions, Tamil literature and palm-leaf manuscripts. Legend holds that during a drought the farmers of the region prayed to Idumban for Lord Murugan's grace, and the rains returned; the ritual of seeking Idumban's blessing for prosperity and fertility continues today. The complex includes shrines to Siddhi Vinayagar and Idumban, and the Thannasi cave shrine named after a saint of the Siddhar mystic order. Devotees may climb the flight of stairs or drive to the portico at the top (parking available at the base) and climb only about 25 steps.

name: Thindal Murugan Temple (Arulmigu Velayudha Swamy Thirukovil)

town_description: Thindal is a suburb on the outskirts of Erode in western Tamil Nadu, on the Erode-Coimbatore (Perundurai) highway. Erode is a major textile and turmeric-trading city on the Kaveri river, and Thindal Malai's hillock with its golden gopuram is a landmark visible from the highway.
